HOW IT WORKS

Move every invoice from sent to settled

Getting paid faster begins with a clear invoice and continues with disciplined payment tracking. Invoice Next connects each recorded payment to the correct invoice, updates the outstanding balance, and keeps the next action visible without relying on disconnected spreadsheets.

01

Send a complete invoice

Give the customer a clear total, exact due date, payment terms, and the instructions needed to pay.

02

Record the payment received

Open the related invoice and enter the received amount, payment date, method, and useful transaction reference.

03

Confirm the remaining balance

Apply a full or partial payment and verify that the outstanding amount and invoice status update correctly.

04

Monitor and follow up

Review unpaid and overdue invoices, check payment history, and contact customers with accurate balance information.

FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

Questions about get paid faster

Can I record partial payments?

Yes. Record the amount received against the correct invoice and keep the unpaid remainder visible until the balance is settled.

Does Invoice Next process PayPal or card payments directly?

The verified product workflow records and tracks payments received through your chosen external payment method. This page does not claim built-in PayPal or card processing.

What payment information should I record?

Record the received date, amount, payment method, and a useful transaction or bank reference whenever those details are available.

Can I see the remaining balance?

Yes. Full and partial payment entries are reflected against the invoice so the outstanding amount remains visible.

How does an invoice become overdue?

An invoice is overdue when its due date has passed and an outstanding balance remains. Always verify recent payments or disputes before following up.

Can I review payment history?

Payment entries remain connected to the relevant invoice, creating a clearer record of what was requested, what was received, and what is still due.
